pages.name: profile-pinned
pages.text:
Knuckles-Team agent platform

A governed runtime for building agents, connecting operational systems, and turning every action into durable, explainable knowledge.

  

Public specification status · Repositories and skills · Contribution guide

Five core projects

The five core projects are Graph OS, Agent Web UI, Agent Utilities, Epistemic Graph, and Agent Connector SDK. Agent Web UI provides the browser operator surface through Graph OS. MCP, REST, and A2A clients use the same governed Graph OS boundary. Graph OS composes the runtime and delegates agent work to the Agent Utilities control plane. Epistemic Graph commits durable knowledge, evidence, provenance, and reasoning results. Source systems connect through the governed Agent Connector SDK contract.

Graph OS

The public runtime gateway: MCP, REST, A2A, identity, policy, fleet composition, and WebUI hosting.

Documentation · Build status

	
Agent Web UI

The browser operator experience for conversations, approvals, tool activity, and graph-backed work.

Documentation · Build status



Agent Utilities

The agent control plane: agents, workflows, evaluation, skills, and governed execution.

Documentation · Build status

	
Epistemic Graph

The reasoning and durable knowledge engine for graph, RDF, SQL, vectors, time, blobs, evidence, and provenance.

Documentation · Capability status



Agent Connector SDK

The governed source-integration boundary for connector identity, discovery, synchronization, replay, and write-back.

Documentation · Build status

Additional operator surfaces

Agent Terminal UI and GeniusBot are additional operator surfaces on the same Graph OS boundary, outside the five core projects. Graph OS also hosts messaging channels.

Agent Terminal UI

The terminal operator surface for the Graph OS REST interface.

Documentation · Build status

	
GeniusBot

The desktop cockpit for specialist agents, embedded terminals, tool approvals, and graph-backed exploration.

Documentation · Build status

Start at the runtime door

Graph OS is the governed runtime entry point. With Python 3.12+ and uv installed, launch the zero-infrastructure local profile:

uvx --from graph-os setup-config generate --profile tiny
uvx --from graph-os graph-os --transport stdio

The generated profile starts with local, bounded defaults. Continue with the Graph OS quick start for provider configuration, Agent Web UI hosting, messaging, and authenticated network transports.

Follow the flow
If you want to…	Start here
Run the platform or connect an MCP/A2A client	Graph OS documentation
Use the browser experience	Agent Web UI documentation
Build agents, workflows, evaluations, or skills	Agent Utilities documentation
Query or operate the knowledge engine directly	Epistemic Graph documentation
Build or certify a source connector	Agent Connector SDK documentation

Every repository documents its own contract and links back to this same runtime map. The boundaries are deliberate: Graph OS is the door, Agent Utilities controls agent behavior, Epistemic Graph owns durable knowledge and reasoning, Agent Web UI presents the browser surface, and Agent Connector SDK governs source integration.

Project health

Build and release evidence lives with the component that owns it. Use each repository's Actions page for current CI and its Pages Status or Capabilities section for shipped behavior. Public issues and pull requests are tracked in the owning repository so operational and design discussions retain their architectural context.

The organization specification report collects owner-native public specs across the core repositories and related public owners. Filter to SPECIFIED to find published work waiting to be built; delivery and acceptance are separate states. The contribution guide links the shared graph-os-development and spec skills.

Contribute from a public spec

Pick an open requirement in the specification status report, then read its owner repository's spec.md, requirements.md, plan.md, test-spec.md, tasks.md, and status.json. The owner repo defines the implementation; related repository specs describe consumers and interfaces. Bootstrap with graph-os-development, then use universal-skills: spec-generator, task-planner, sdd-implementer, spec-verifier, and sdd-full-lifecycle. The step-by-step guide covers local setup, reuse, tests, pull requests, and public evidence.

All five core projects are released under the MIT License.

pages.name: index
pages.text:
Graph OS ecosystem

Build agents and connect source systems through Graph OS, with Epistemic Graph as the durable knowledge engine.

Specification statusRepositories and skillsContributeOrganization profile
Start with work waiting to be built

The public specification report lists owner-native specs, the share of requirements each has delivered, and the requirements still open. Expand a specification to pick one. Each owner repository holds the full design, implementation tasks, and test contract. A status claim needs public evidence; publication alone does not mean implementation or acceptance.

Contribute with the shared skills

Choose an unbuilt requirement, read its owner spec.md, plan.md, test-spec.md, tasks.md, and status.json, then bootstrap your environment with graph-os-development. Install universal-skills and use its spec-generator, task-planner, sdd-implementer, spec-verifier, or sdd-full-lifecycle. Reuse owner components, run repository tests and CCCC, jscpd, Dupehound, and KISS checks, submit a pull request, and update status only with public merged and test evidence. Read the full contribution path.

Five core projects

Graph OS is the governed runtime gateway. It hosts Agent Web UI and delegates agent work to Agent Utilities; Epistemic Graph owns durable knowledge, and Agent Connector SDK governs source integration.

Graph OS — runtime and gateway.
Epistemic Graph — durable knowledge and reasoning.
Agent Connector SDK — governed connector contracts.
Agent Utilities — agent orchestration.
Agent Web UI — browser experience.
Additional operator surfaces

Agent Terminal UI and GeniusBot use the same Graph OS boundary and are outside the five core projects.

Agent Terminal UI — terminal operator surface for the Graph OS REST interface.
GeniusBot — desktop cockpit.
Related contributor repositories
Repository Manager — workspace lifecycle.
Pipelines — shared CI and release workflows.
Emerald Exchange — exchange integration.
Tunnel Manager — tunnel lifecycle.
Universal Skills — shared spec, development, architecture, and verification skills.

pages.name: skills
pages.text:
Graph OS repositories and skills
EcosystemSpec statusContribute

universal-skills distributes the shared contributor skills. The Graph OS package contains the canonical ecosystem development skill and its public bootstrap recipe. The universal-skills entry makes that canonical skill discoverable before Graph OS is installed.

Install the skill kit with pip install universal-skills and install-skills --all-detected --symlink. Read a chosen repository's AGENTS.md and all five owner spec files before building: spec.md, plan.md, test-spec.md, tasks.md, and status.json. The contribution guide gives the full path from a public checkout to a PR.

Which skill to use
Stage	Skill	Use it for
Orient and bootstrap	graph-os-development	Choose the owner, clone public sources, reuse existing wiring, and follow repository gates.
Engine work	epistemic-graph-development	Apply Epistemic Graph engine and client conventions after finding an engine-owned spec.
Specify	spec-generator	Write a complete public owner contract from a feature request.
Design	c4-architecture	Describe system boundaries and the components a design reuses.
Plan and implement	task-planner and sdd-implementer	Turn spec acceptance into ordered changes and implement them.
Test and verify	automated-test-runner and spec-verifier	Run repository checks and verify design, tests, and public evidence.
Full sequence	sdd-full-lifecycle	Coordinate specification through accepted delivery.
Where the code lives

The organization hub owns the cross-repository map, status report, and governance. Each deliverable is implemented in the repository named by its owner spec. Related specs describe consumers and interfaces; a disputed owner stays unresolved until its contract is reviewed.

Five core projects

Graph OS is the governed runtime gateway. It hosts Agent Web UI and delegates agent work to Agent Utilities; Epistemic Graph owns durable knowledge, and Agent Connector SDK governs source integration.

Graph OS — runtime and gateway.
Agent Web UI — browser experience.
Agent Utilities — agent orchestration.
Epistemic Graph — durable knowledge and reasoning.

Agent Terminal UI and GeniusBot use the same Graph OS boundary and are outside the five core projects.

Agent Terminal UI — terminal operator surface for the Graph OS REST interface.

Repository Manager owns workspace lifecycle; Pipelines owns shared CI and release workflows; Emerald Exchange owns exchange integration; Tunnel Manager owns tunnel lifecycle; and Universal Skills provides shared contributor skills.
